ce_bugs.text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Attendees are committed before the calendar update, so a provider failure leaves durable split-brain state that the same request cannot retry because the guests now look duplicated.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — Calendar updates use the caller's credentials instead of the included booking owner's credentials, so authorized attendee or team-admin calls can fail after the database commit or target the wrong calendar account.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The server accepts an unbounded guest array, allowing any authorized caller to force arbitrarily large database writes, calendar payloads, and outbound-email fan-out.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:54 — The endpoint never rejects cancelled, rejected, or past bookings, so a direct caller can mutate terminal bookings and emit confirmed calendar invitations for them.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The input contract accepts duplicate and case-variant emails, allowing direct callers to create duplicate attendees and inconsistent calendar state.
apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 — The fallback error message is dead code because the preceding template literal is always truthy.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The uncapped guests array lets one request trigger unbounded attendee creation plus calendar and email fan-out over the enlarged attendee list.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — Calendar synchronization runs after the attendee commit, so a transient provider failure leaves partial state that the same request cannot retry

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Treating every attendee as authorized lets any invited guest add arbitrary recipients and disclose the booking's calendar and video-call details to them.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — Comparing the raw guest address against a lowercased blacklist lets callers bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS with case variants.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The unbounded guest array turns this mutation into an authenticated bulk-email and resource-exhaustion primitive against arbitrary recipient addresses.

mrv_findings.text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — (P1, confidence 100) `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` — Calendar synchronization is owned by the invoking attendee or team administrator instead of the booking organizer, so authorized non-organizer callers update with the wrong calendar credentials and can leave the organizer’s event unchanged.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — (P1, confidence 100) `const bookingAttendees = await prisma.booking.update({` — The attendee rows are committed before the external calendar update at line 165, so a calendar failure returns an error after durable mutation and a retry cannot repair the calendar because the guests are then treated as already present.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — (P1, confidence 100) `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(` — This filter never deduplicates entries within the request, so a direct API call with repeated addresses either creates duplicate attendee rows or makes the entire createMany fail if the database enforces uniqueness.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — (P2, confidence 100) `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` — Passing the unfiltered request instead of `uniqueGuests` misclassifies any already-present address resubmitted alongside a new guest as newly added and sends it the scheduled-attendee email.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — (P1, confidence 100) `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` — The API permits an unbounded guest array that is fully materialized, inserted, translated, calendar-synchronized, and emailed synchronously, creating a request-size scalability cliff on a hot mutation.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 — (P2, confidence 100) `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) {` — Membership is checked by a linear array scan inside the full-attendee loop, making notification classification quadratic for the unbounded lists accepted by the endpoint instead of using a Set.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:549 — (P1, confidence 100) `await Promise.all(emailsToSend);` — One provider rejection aborts the aggregate while sibling sends continue, and the caller suppresses that rejection and returns success, leaving a silently partial notification fanout with no retry boundary.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:531 — (P2, confidence 100) `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) {` — The sole new caller constructs `evt` without a `team` field, so this intended team-member notification path is structurally unreachable for team bookings.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:60 — (P1, confidence 75) `id: booking.userId || 0,` — The handler models every booking as having a single organizer user even though `userId` is nullable, so valid team-owned bookings fail before guests can be added instead of resolving ownership through the booking’s actual host model.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — (P1, confidence 75) `const bookingAttendees = await prisma.booking.update({` — The mutation has no booking-status or time guard, so cancelled, rejected, or already-ended bookings can transition back into calendar and email activity despite being terminal historical records.

docs/tasks/task-001.md:2 — (P1, confidence 100) `Review the change.` — The task supplies no acceptance criteria or verification for authorization, lifecycle eligibility, duplicate handling, calendar synchronization, or notification outcomes, so completion cannot be objectively established.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — (P1, confidence 75) `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` — The server contract omits uniqueness validation, so direct API callers can submit repeated addresses and trigger duplicate attendees/notifications or an avoidable persistence failure.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — (P1, confidence 100) `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` — A mixed request containing an existing attendee and a genuinely new guest passes the unfiltered input to notification classification, causing the existing attendee to be treated as newly added and receive the wrong scheduled-email path.

apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx:194 — (P1, confidence 100) `id: "add_members",` — The new action is included in the edit menu that line 554 renders for past confirmed bookings, so an elapsed event can still be mutated and fresh calendar invitations sent with no lifecycle guard.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:39 — (P3, confidence 100) `setMultiEmailValue([""]);` — Success resets the inputs but not `isInvalidEmail`, so after correcting an invalid entry and succeeding, reopening the dialog immediately shows a stale validation error.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — (P1, confidence 100) `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` — This external-calendar call runs only after the attendee rows are committed, so a provider failure returns an error after the local change and the retry is rejected as having no unique guests, leaving the calendar update impossible to recover through this command.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — (P1, confidence 75) `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` — The handler explicitly permits non-organizer attendees and team operators, but then attempts to update the organizer-owned calendar using the caller's credentials, so those allowed invocation paths cannot reliably reach the integration that owns the booking event.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:54 — (P1, confidence 75) `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) {` — Treating any attendee as authorized lets a low-privilege participant mutate the organizer’s booking and invite arbitrary external addresses, exposing event and video-call details without organizer approval.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — (P2, confidence 100) `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` — The unbounded guest array lets an authenticated caller force bulk database inserts, calendar updates, translation work, and email fan-out, enabling resource exhaustion and invitation spam.
